# .NET MAUI

- MAU-011 (must): In a MAUI window's lifecycle events: on Stopped, disconnect from any long running processes, or cancel any pending requests that might consume device resources, because there's no guarantee the app will resume (the operating system may terminate it). On Resumed, subscribe to any required events and refresh any content that's on the visible page. On Destroying, remove any event subscriptions attached to the native window. On iOS and Mac Catalyst, any string state should be persisted to the State property of the Backgrounding event's BackgroundingEventArgs. In the Android activity lifecycle overrides that need it, such as OnPause and OnDestroy, always call the super class's implementation.
